blocks.en:
Nitrogen dioxide ( NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} ) is a common air pollutant, released into the atmosphere through the incomplete burning of fossil fuels, and associated with respiratory and cardiovascular diseases in humans. Ambient NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} concentrations are regulated through air-quality limits assessed with a sparse network of fixed monitors European Environment Agency (2026) . The revised EU Ambient Air Quality Directive (2024/2881) introduces a daily NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} limit to be met from 2030 European Parliament and Council of the European Union (2024) .
At present, neither the regulatory monitoring network nor existing coarse, annual-mean models can resolve NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} concentrations at the spatio-temporal resolutions necessary to assess compliance Cooper et al. (2020) ; Larkin et al. (2017) ; Shen et al. (2022) . Here we map NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} across Europe at hourly and 10 m 10\text{\,}\mathrm{m} resolution with a machine-learning model that combines ground monitors with satellite, reanalysis, land-use, traffic and emission data and returns a calibrated predictive distribution at every location. Validated against held-out regulatory monitors European Environment Agency (2026) and independent citizen-science campaigns De Craemer et al. (2019) ; Lauriks et al. (2022) , the maps resolve high-resolution spatiotemporal NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} gradients for 110 metropolitan areas in Europe. We reconstruct the daily compliance statistic across those regions and find limit breaches in 91 EU air quality zones deemed compliant by the regulatory monitoring network, covering a population of approximately 135 M. Beyond air quality zones and monitor locations, an estimated 9- 9.4 9.4 % (20 M) of the population in mapped regions lives in areas where the daily NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} limit is breached.
The high-resolution maps offer a route to population-scale assessment of compliance with the 2030 limits.

blocks.en: Nitrogen dioxide ( NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} ) is a common air pollutant to which hundreds of millions of people are exposed every day. It forms through the incomplete burning of fossil fuels, at the exhaust of road vehicles and from power generation, industry and shipping Organization and others (2021) . Short-term exposure inflames the airways while sustained exposure is associated with impaired lung development in children, cardiovascular disease and premature death Atkinson et al. (2018) ; Nitschke (1999) ; Gillespie-Bennett et al. (2011) ; Khaniabadi et al. (2017) . Additionally, NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} tracks the broader mixture of traffic-related pollutants that carry much of the health burden that can be attributed to air-pollution Beckerman et al. (2008) . Because these effects begin at concentrations common in European cities, the World Health Organization sharply lowered its recommended NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} guideline in 2021 Organization and others (2021) .

blocks.en: Managing the risks of air pollution depends on knowing where and when they occur, while NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} concentration is highly variable across space and follows distinct temporal patterns at seasonal, weekly and diurnal frequencies Lebret et al. (2000) ; Domínguez-López et al. (2014) . Its concentration can drop by tens of µ ​ g m − 3 \mathrm{\SIUnitSymbolMicro g}\text{\,}{\mathrm{m}}^{-3} over a few tens of metres and drastically varies between rush hour and clear roads. Personal exposure is therefore determined by the precise locations where people live, work and travel Monn (2001) . Regulatory assessment, however, rests on a sparse network of fixed reference monitors European Environment Agency (2023) , and compliance is assessed in administrative air quality zones European Parliament and Council of the European Union (2024) , from a limited number of representative sampling points. The air most people actually breathe, and whether it meets the legal limits, remains largely unmeasured.

blocks.en:
The revised European Union (EU) Ambient Air Quality Directive (2024/2881) European Parliament and Council of the European Union (2024) moves European standards towards the 2021 WHO guidance, tightening the NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} limits that must be met from 2030 on. Alongside the existing hourly and annual limits, it introduces a daily limit. The 24-hour mean may exceed 50 µ ​ g m − 3 \mathrm{\SIUnitSymbolMicro g}\text{\,}{\mathrm{m}}^{-3} on no more than 18 days per year. Unlike the long-standing annual and one-hour limits, compliance with the daily limit has not been mapped or modeled at continental scale. Moreover, it increasingly constitutes the limit that is hardest to meet: as ambient NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} has fallen across Europe over the past decades Geddes et al. (2015) , the annual limit currently in force (40 µ ​ g m − 3 \mathrm{\SIUnitSymbolMicro g}\text{\,}{\mathrm{m}}^{-3} , to be lowered to 20 µ ​ g m − 3 \mathrm{\SIUnitSymbolMicro g}\text{\,}{\mathrm{m}}^{-3} from 2030) and the one-hour limit (200 µ ​ g m − 3 \mathrm{\SIUnitSymbolMicro g}\text{\,}{\mathrm{m}}^{-3} ) are not exceeded at a large majority of reference stations. We find that locations that breach the daily exposure limit are frequently compliant with the annual and hourly limits.
The EU Directive identifies air-quality modeling as a complementary means of locating non-compliance European Parliament and Council of the European Union (2024) , yet existing products are either spatially too coarse to resolve within-city gradients that determine exposure Cooper et al. (2022) ; Geddes et al. (2015) ; Cooper et al. (2020) , or temporally too coarse (typically annual or monthly means) to reconstruct daily statistics Larkin et al. (2017) ; Shen et al. (2022) ; Scheibenreif et al. (2022) .

blocks.en: Assessing where the daily limit is breached therefore demands estimates that are both fine-grained enough to capture street-scale gradients and temporally complete enough to reconstruct a daily mean for each day of the year. Here we present NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} maps at hourly resolution and 10 m 10\text{\,}\mathrm{m} ground sampling distance (GSD) across Europe. We use machine learning to fuse the observations of the regulatory network with satellite observations, atmospheric reanalysis and fine-scale land-use, traffic and emission data, to produce spatially continuous, uncertainty-calibrated maps of NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} concentration. Based on these maps, we assess where the new daily limit is exceeded. At the level of regulatory air quality zones, we identify NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} concentrations above the limit in 161 zones, 91 of which are deemed compliant by the current regulatory network.
blocks.zh: 因此,要评估日限被突破之处,就需要估算出足够精细的、足以反映街道梯度和时间上足够完整的数据,以重建每年每一天的日均值。 我们在此展示NO 2\text{NO\vphantom\text}\text{2}按小时分辨率绘制的地图和10 m 10\text\,\ { mathrm{ m} 整个欧洲的地面采样距离。 我们利用机器学习将监管网络的观测与卫星观测、大气再分析和精细规模的土地利用、交通和排放数据结合起来,制作NO 2\text{NO\vphantom\text}\smash[t]\text{2}浓度的空间连续、不确定性校准地图。 根据这些地图,我们评估新的日限在哪些地方被超越。 在空气质量监管区一级,我们发现NO 2\text{NO\vphantom\text_smash{text{2}在161个区超过限值的浓度,其中91个区被目前的监管网络认为符合要求。

blocks.en: 1.1 NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} modeling approach
blocks.zh: 1.1 NO 2\ text{NO\vphantom\ text}\ smash[t]\ text{2}\\x 建模方法

blocks.en:
Ambient NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} concentrations across Europe are modeled based on the NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} record of the European Environment Agency’s air-quality monitoring network European Environment Agency (2026) for the years 2018–2023. We cross-reference a dataset of 152 152 M station-hours with a diverse set of covariates that contain determinants of NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} pollution such as road networks, buildings, terrain and population data as well as meteorological and atmospheric reanalysis data (see Tab. 1 for the full list of covariates). We frame NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} modelling as a sparsely-supervised dense regression problem and propose a deep ensemble model to estimate NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} concentrations from the multi-modal input data stack. In order to assess compliance with the EU’s daily NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} limit, high-resolution estimates are required. We therefore model NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} at hourly temporal and 10 m 10\text{\,}\mathrm{m} spatial resolution. In this setting, the compute cost to cover large regions over annual time-spans ( 365 × 24 365\times 24 predictions per pixel per year) quickly becomes prohibitive. To mitigate it, our factored U-net model processes data in a patch-wise fashion and, unlike established pixel-wise approaches Kim et al. (2021) , produces NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} estimates for 1.28 × 1.28 1.28\times 1.28 km areas at a time, at 10 m 10\text{\,}\mathrm{m} resolution. Additionally, the NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} field is factorised into static spatial bases and temporally varying coefficients, which amortises the expensive processing of high-resolution spatial inputs over a full year of hourly temporal coefficients (Fig. 1 , see Sec. 2.2 for details). The model is trained on ≈ 85 \approx 85 % of the monitoring locations (127 M station-hours) and evaluated on the remaining 15% of locations (25 M station-hours), where it outperforms pixel-wise and reanalysis-based baselines (Tab. 2 ) and reaches an RMSE of 11.32 ± 0.26 11.32\pm 0.26 µ ​ g m − 3 \mathrm{\SIUnitSymbolMicro g}\text{\,}{\mathrm{m}}^{-3} and R2-score of 0.571 ± 0.013 0.571\pm 0.013 . The model accurately reconstructs temporal patterns of NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} concentration across different time scales (Figs. 8 , 9 , 10 ) and corresponds well to high-resolution spatial patterns established in independent citizen science campaigns De Craemer et al. (2019) ; Lauriks et al. (2022) in Flanders 2018 (RMSE 4.25 4.25 µ ​ g m − 3 \mathrm{\SIUnitSymbolMicro g}\text{\,}{\mathrm{m}}^{-3} , R2-score 0.562 0.562 ) and Brussels 2021 (RMSE 5.05 5.05 µ ​ g m − 3 \mathrm{\SIUnitSymbolMicro g}\text{\,}{\mathrm{m}}^{-3} , R2-score 0.470 0.470 ).
To facilitate interpretation of the model’s NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} estimates, we also provide estimates of both aleatoric uncertainty (obtained through training with a Gaussian log-likelihood loss Nix and Weigend (1994) ) and epistemic uncertainty (obtained from the spread between ensemble members Lakshminarayanan et al. (2017) ). Together, they specify a calibrated predictive distribution per pixel (Fig. 11 , see Sec. 2.2 ), which we utilise for a probabilistic assessment of where the mapped values exceed the regulatory limit.

blocks.en: 1.2 Limit breach detection
blocks.zh: 1.2 限制破损探测

blocks.en:
The EU’s daily NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} limit is breached if, within a year, more than 18 days are recorded with a 24-hour mean NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} concentration above 50 µ ​ g m − 3 \mathrm{\SIUnitSymbolMicro g}\text{\,}{\mathrm{m}}^{-3} . We assess compliance with the regulatory limit based on two statistics reconstructed from our model’s full hourly NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} timeseries.
The expected non-compliance statistic computes the expected number of days exceeding 50 µ ​ g m − 3 \mathrm{\SIUnitSymbolMicro g}\text{\,}{\mathrm{m}}^{-3} from the modeled hourly predictive mean and variance.
Additionally, we derive the probability of non-compliance as the probability of observing more than 18 days above 50 µ ​ g m − 3 \mathrm{\SIUnitSymbolMicro g}\text{\,}{\mathrm{m}}^{-3} based on the predictive uncertainty of the model (see Sec. 2.2 for details).

Of 3060 3060 EEA stations reporting NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} in 2023, 264 264 breach the daily limit. The 110 mapped regions (Fig. 7 ) are home to 215 M people, roughly 40% of the EU-27(+UK) population.
Our expected exceedance statistic finds 20.15 M people (9.4%) affected by a 24-hour-limit breach, and 19.49 M (9.1%) live in areas with a probability of non-compliance greater than 50%. Exposure shows strong geographic patterns, concentrated in southern-European conurbations (Fig. 5 Madrid 4.5 M, the Po Valley 3.2 M, Barcelona, Rome, Turin, Athens) together with London and Paris, while the large northern metropolitan regions (Rhine-Ruhr, Randstad, the English Midlands, Upper Silesia) show essentially no 24-hour-limit breaches.

blocks.en: Breach days are heavily concentrated in the winter, with 54% of observed breach-days in November–February and a clear minimum in May–August. Breach days are also not temporally independent: 78% of observed breach-days occur in a run of ≥ 2 \geq 2 consecutive days. Long runs of 6 or more days account for 26% of all breaches. Within the mapped regions, the number of exceedance days per pixel is heavily skewed to the left, with 5.4% of mapped pixels exceeding the limit on at least one day of the year, but only 0.41% exceeding it on more than 18 days. Breaches are concentrated in a small set of roadside hotspot pixels that exceed the limit on 100–270 days of the year.

blocks.en: Overall, we find that exceedance of the 24-hour limit is not a diffuse, year-round phenomenon but tends to occur in marked, spatially and seasonally concentrated multi-day episodes, with direct implications for the health burden.

blocks.en:
We also examined how close currently-compliant zones are to the NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} limit, based on both the regulatory network’s measurement and the model’s probabilistic risk. Of the 225 officially-compliant, monitored zones in our mapped footprint, 78 (35%) have at least one monitor whose own 19 th -highest daily mean already falls within [ 40 , 50 ) [40,50) µ ​ g m − 3 \mathrm{\SIUnitSymbolMicro g}\text{\,}{\mathrm{m}}^{-3} , i.e., less than 10 µ ​ g m − 3 \mathrm{\SIUnitSymbolMicro g}\text{\,}{\mathrm{m}}^{-3} from the limit. The remaining 147 (65%) have a larger margin to the limit, remaining below 40 40 µ ​ g m − 3 \mathrm{\SIUnitSymbolMicro g}\text{\,}{\mathrm{m}}^{-3} .
The EU Directive treats air-quality modeling as a complementary tool for locating non-compliance. We find that the model’s disagreement with the regulatory network concentrates where the official measurements are already close to the limit. Of 78 zones that are at most 10 µ ​ g m − 3 \mathrm{\SIUnitSymbolMicro g}\text{\,}{\mathrm{m}}^{-3} below the limit according to the official statistics, 43 (55%) are flagged in our map as breaching the limit. This share rises to 71% for zones that are within 5 µ ​ g m − 3 \mathrm{\SIUnitSymbolMicro g}\text{\,}{\mathrm{m}}^{-3} of the limit. blocks.zh: 2 方法

blocks.en: 2.1 Datasets
blocks.zh: 2.1 数据集

blocks.en:
We model ambient NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} concentrations across Europe at hourly resolution. Ground truth is the hourly NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} record of the European Environment Agency’s air-quality monitoring network European Environment Agency (2026) for the years 2018–2023, comprising 3823 3823 reference stations spanning urban-traffic, urban-background, suburban and rural site types. Each supervised example corresponds to a single station–hour pair. We collect a dataset of 152 152 M station–hours across Europe.
The dataset is restricted to observations of hourly NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} concentrations that are tagged as valid with verification by the local reporting authority. Additionally, measurements below zero and spikes above 500 µ ​ g m − 3 \mathrm{\SIUnitSymbolMicro g}\text{\,}{\mathrm{m}}^{-3} are not considered.
blocks.zh:
我们模拟环境 NO 2\text{NO\vphantom\text\text\tsmash[t]\text{2}以小时分辨率在欧洲各地的浓度。 地面真相是2018-2023年欧洲环境局空气质量监测网络(2026年)的每小时NO NO\text{NOvphantom\text{stext}记录,包括3823个参考站,涵盖城市交通、城市背景、郊区和农村地点类型。 每个受监管的例子都对应一个单一的车站时数对. 我们收集了全欧洲152M站每小时的数据集。
数据集仅限于小时NO 2\text{NO\vphantom\text}\smash{t}\text{2}浓度的观测,这些浓度被标记为有效的,由当地报告当局进行核实。 此外,测量值低于零,峰值超过500 μg m − 3\mathrm SIUnitSymbolMicro gQQQText\, \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ 不考虑 。

blocks.en: For every station-hour observation from the EEA network we collect a stack of multi-modal covariates colocated with the monitor, resampled to 10 m 10\text{\,}\mathrm{m} resolution and covering an area of 1.28 × 1.28 km 1.28\times$1.28\text{\,}\mathrm{km}$ around the monitor. Predictors combine temporally static land-use, emission and topographic descriptors with dynamic reanalysis and satellite data that vary at different temporal frequencies (see Tab. 1 for the full list of covariates).
blocks.zh: 每一次EEA网络的台时观测,我们都会收集一叠与显示器同座的多模式共变物,再被复制到10 m 10\text~,}\mathrm{m}分辨率,覆盖面积1.28×1.28 km 1.28\text~,}\mathrm{km}在显示器周围. 预测器将时间静止的土地使用、排放和地形描述符与动态再分析和卫星数据结合起来,这些数据在不同的时间频率上有所不同(关于共变物的完整清单,见附件1)。

blocks.en:
We distinguish static per-pixel layers that capture fine-scale determinants of the NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} field (street canyons, the road network, buildings, terrain, population), and dynamic layers with meteorological and photochemical information (wind speed and direction, boundary layer, temperature, regional emissions and satellite NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} observations) that modulate concentrations over time. Additionally, we derive dynamic terms such as an ”is-weekend” indicator, a normalized day-of-year, a year index, geolocation encodings, an Sentinel-5P-missing mask and a 7-day Sentinel-5P backfill. We also derive additional covariates from static data sources.
The elevation data Strobl (2020) is projected to different scales by a discrete wavelet decomposition and independent reconstruction of the coefficients to 12 scale-specific elevation maps ( 30 m 30\text{\,}\mathrm{m} – 122.9 km 122.9\text{\,}\mathrm{km} , as proposed in Kim et al. (2021) ).
We obtain vector layers from OpenStreetMap OpenStreetMap contributors (2017) (roads by class, buildings, land use, water aeroway, ports) and rasterize them independently into binary maps.
AlphaEarth embeddings are dequantized according to their usage instructions Brown et al. (2025) .
The annual-average-daily-traffic data Shen et al. (2024) is accumulated within nested buffer radii ( 50 – 5000 m 505000\text{\,}\mathrm{m} ) around each pixel.
We utilize the following variables from ERA5 Hersbach et al. (2020) : total precipitation (TP), boundary layer height (BLH), clear-sky direct solar radiation (CDIR), temperature at 2m (T2M) and wind (U10,V10).

blocks.en: Land-use predictors that are heavy-tailed or non-negative are transformed per-channel with a fitted Yeo–Johnson power transform Weisberg (2001) followed by z-score standardization (TP, BLH, CDIR, CAMS NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} reanalysis and emissions, population density, traffic data and the target NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} measurement). Roughly symmetric covariates are z-score standardized (T2M, U10, V10, DEM incl. wavelet levels). The geospatial embeddings, binary OSM and WorldCover maps as well as time and location encodings are left in their native scale. Normalization statistics are estimated once on the training split and applied unchanged to validation, test and inference data.

blocks.en: Monitoring stations are partitioned into distinct training, validation and test sets. Each station is described by its static context: coordinates, population, distance to the nearest major road, the DEM/wavelet terrain data, and its long-run mean observed NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} . These features are standardized, log-transformed where skewed, reduced to five dimensions with UMAP McInnes et al. (2018) and clustered with HDBSCAN McInnes et al. (2017) (following the approach by Kim et al. (2021) ). Within each cluster the stations are drawn at random into 70% training, 15% validation and 15% test, so every split carries the same mixture of station environments (Fig. 6 ). In addition, we filter for locations with at least 365 days carrying ≥ 18 \geq 18 hourly values together with plausible statistics (mean, standard deviation and 99 th percentile below 100 100 , 30 30 and 200 200 µ ​ g m − 3 \mathrm{\SIUnitSymbolMicro g}\text{\,}{\mathrm{m}}^{-3} , respectively).
blocks.zh: 监测站分为不同的培训、鉴定和测试组。 每个站台均以其静态背景描述:坐标,人口,距离最近的干道,DEM/波浪地形数据,以及其长期观测的NO 2\text{NO\vphantom\text_smash[t]\text{2}}}. 这些特征是标准化的,在偏斜之处转换日志,与UMAP McInnes等人(2018年)缩小为5维,与HDBSCAN McInnes等人(2017年)集群(遵循Kim等人(2021年)的做法)。 在每个组群中,各站点随机抽取到70%的培训、15%的验证和15%的测试,因此,每个分块都搭载同样的站点环境混合体(图6)。 此外,我们对至少365天载有18 \ \ eq 18小时值的地点进行过滤,并附上可信的统计数据(平均,标准偏差和低于100、30和200 200 μg m - 3\ mathrm的99 百分位数) SIUnitSymbolMicro gQQQText\, \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \

blocks.en:
For independent evaluation we use NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} datasets from passive sampler campaigns that are not part of the regulatory network. These are the citizen-science CurieuzeNeuzen campaign in Flanders from May 2018 with 17 886 17\,886 diffusion tube NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} concentration measurements De Craemer et al. (2019) and the CurieuzenAir campaign in Brussels Lauriks et al. (2022) (25 September–23 October 2021, ≈ \approx 2,493 tubes).
Passive samplers integrate NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} over a multi-week window, so the corresponding model estimate is the mean prediction over the same window at the sampler location. These campaigns provide high spatial coverage relative to the regulatory network, however the geo-location of each diffusion tube is only known to street level to ensure data privacy.
blocks.zh:
对于独立的评价,我们使用NO 2\text{NO\vphantom\text_smash[t]\text{2}来自不属于监管网络的被动采样器运动的数据集。 这些是2018年5月起在佛兰德举办的公民-科学 Curieuze Neuzen 运动,使用 17 886 17\ 886 扩散管 NO 2\ text{NO\vphantom\ text_smash[t]\ text{2}浓度测量 De Craemer等人(2019年),以及布鲁塞尔劳里克斯等人(2022年)的CurieuzenAir运动(2021年9月25日至10月23日,QQ\\约2,493管).
被动采样器通过多星期窗口整合NO 2\text{NO\vphantom\text_smash[t]\text{2},因此相应的模型估计是采样器位置同一窗口上的平均预测. 与监管网络相比,这些运动提供了较高的空间覆盖面,但每个扩散管的地理位置仅为街道级别所知,以确保数据隐私。

blocks.en: We cast hourly NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} mapping as a sparsely-supervised dense regression problem. A convolutional network processes the multi-modal data patch and outputs a dense NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} field at 10 m 10\text{\,}\mathrm{m} ground resolution ( 1.28 × 1.28 km 1.28\times$1.28\text{\,}\mathrm{km}$ per patch). The loss is evaluated only at the exact location of the supervising station, via a masked objective. Cases where multiple monitoring stations are located within the same patch are rare but explicitly handled, and every corresponding pixel is supervised. A distinct prediction is produced for every hour of the 2018–2023 record with independent inference steps. At deployment, dense maps are produced per UTM tile at 10 m 10\text{\,}\mathrm{m} and hourly cadence.
blocks.zh: 我们把小时 NO 2\ text{NO\vphantom\ text\smash}\ text{2} 当作一个很少监督的密集回归问题。 演化网络处理多模式数据补丁,输出密集的NO 2\text{NO\vphantom\text}\smash{ text{2} 字段在 10\text\,\ mathrm{ m} 地面分辨率 (1. 28× 1. 28 km 1. 28\tims 1. 28\text\,\ mathrm{ km} $每补丁)。 只有在监督站的确切位置,通过一个蒙面目标对损失进行评估。 在同一补丁内设置多个监测站的病例很少,但明确处理,每个相应的像素都受到监督. 2018–2023年记录的每个小时都会有明显的预测,并有独立的推断步骤. 在部署时,每块UTM瓷砖在10 m 10\text ~,}\mathrm{m}和小时卡登斯生成密集的地图.

blocks.en: We use a factored U-net Ronneberger et al. (2015) model architecture that consists of a three-level encoder–decoder with GroupNorm and SiLU activations. The model maps the patch of static input modalities to a time-invariant spatial baseline field s 0 ​ ( x ) s_{0}(x) and K K spatial mode maps L k ​ ( x ) L_{k}(x) . A small temporal head (implemented as two layer MLP) maps the dynamic inputs at hour t t to K K scalar coefficients c k ​ ( t ) c_{k}(t) . The hourly prediction is their linear combination, y ^ ​ ( x , t ) = s 0 ​ ( x ) + ∑ k = 1 K L k ​ ( x ) ​ c k ​ ( t ) , \hat{y}(x,t)=s_{0}(x)+\sum_{k=1}^{K}L_{k}(x)\,c_{k}(t), (1) implemented with K = 4 K=4 temporal modes (Fig. 1 ). This factorization of the input dataset into static and dynamic components makes dense inference at hourly resolution feasible. The spatial encoder is evaluated only once per location and year, after which any number of hours is reconstructed from the cheap temporal head and the linear combination of temporal coefficients and spatial maps (Eqn. 1 ). This reduces a full year of hourly maps from 365 × 24 365\times 24 forward passes to one spatial pass plus per-hour coefficients (Fig. 1 ).

Continuous maps over an area of interest are produced by tiling the region on its native UTM grid, evaluating the spatial encoder once per tile to obtain the factored basis ( s 0 s_{0} , L k L_{k} , and the log-variance bases), and reconstructing each hour from per-tile-centre dynamic vectors. Per-hour fields are combined into temporal aggregates (e.g. annual or campaign-window means) analytically from the stored basis, and adjacent tiles are seam-blended and mosaicked together. Land-surface masking uses the WorldCover water class Zanaga et al. (2022) .
In total, we map compliance statistics for 110 regions across Europe in 2023 (Fig. 7 ), covering all major metropolitan areas. We selected the EU-27 capital cities, metropolitan regions with over 1 M inhabitants and added smaller cities in the vicinity of already mapped areas (see Tab. 11 for the full list). The covered areas vary in size between 690 690 (Genoa) and 24 287 24\,287 km 2 (Po Valley). Region sizes are selected proportionally to the square-root of the covered population. Where appropriate, individual regions are combined into larger areas (Po Valley, Midlands North, Flanders, Rhine-Rhur, Upper Silesia).

blocks.en: The model covers the different temporal dynamics of NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} well and accurately represents seasonal cycles with highs in the Winter, daily cycles around rush-hour in the morning and evenings (Fig. 10 ), as well as reduced emissions on the weekend relative to the rest of the week (Fig. 8 ). On the annual scale, the model follows the general downward-trend of NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} during the 2018-2023 period (Fig. 9 ). As baselines, we include a constant mean prediction, which yields the highest RMSE in our evaluation, as well as an evaluation of CAMS NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} reanalysis data alone, which already possesses significant skill (R2-score up to 0.41 0.41 ) despite significantly lower spatial resolution. To isolate the effect of spatial context through the multi-modal input patches ( 1.28 × 1.28 1.28\times 1.28 km) we compare the factored U-net ensemble model with a ridge regression Horel (1962) baseline trained on the center pixels of the full multi-modal input patches. blocks.en: Modality selection. In order to achieve the best possible skill at high-resolution NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} estimation, we collect a comprehensive set of input modalities. We reason that the factored U-net ensemble handles potential collinearity between the predictors well, and learns to disregard uninformative modalities. We test this in a leave-one-out ablation study, where the model is re-trained on subsets of the input modalities (Tab. 5 ). We find that, even in the presence of all other modalities, some individual modalities are extraordinarily important for NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} estimation performance. The AlphaEarth embeddings are the most important static input, while CAMS is the most important dynamic modality. Only the GRIP4 road network and GHSL population data have a significant negative effect on overall performance. However, both of these modalities have direct analogues in the remaining dataset (WorldPop and the street network rasterized from OSM).
blocks.zh: 模式选择。 为了在高清 NO 2\text{NO\vphantom\text}\smash[t]\text{2}的估算中达到最佳技能,我们收集了一套全面的输入模式. 我们的理由是,纳入系数的U-net组合能很好地处理预测器之间的潜在对齐性,并学会忽略非信息化模式。 我们在一项 " 一停而出 " 的研究中测试了这一点,在该研究中,该模型在输入模式的子集上重新培训(第5段)。 我们发现,即使存在所有其他模式,一些单个模式对于NO 2\text{NO\vphantom\text}\smash[t]\text{2}估计性能来说,也具有特别重要的意义。 阿尔法地球嵌入是最重要的静态输入,而CAMS则是最重要的动态模式. 只有GRIP4公路网络和GHSL人口数据对总体绩效产生重大不利影响. 然而,这两种模式在剩余的数据集中都有直接的模拟(WorldPop和街道网络由OSM光线化).

blocks.en: We quantify the quality the proposed expected and probabilistic breach statistics on the held-out regulatory monitors (Tab. 9 ). Both statistics exhibit high precision ( 0.892 0.892 and 0.927 0.927 , respectively). This indicates that detected limit breaches correspond to true breaches with high likelihood (Fig. 12 , left). However, the statistics also underestimate the total number of breaches. Across 2488 station-years, our hold-out dataset contains 358 true annual limit breaches, 234 − 236 234-236 , of which are not detected (recall 0.341 − 0.346 0.341-0.346 ). The reported number of breaches is therefore a conservative lower bound on the total number of breaching 10 m 10\text{\,}\mathrm{m} 2 locations in the mapped regions. We compare the probabilistic metrics with the deterministic count of days above the exposure limit computed from the modeled hourly timeseries ( ∑ d = 1 D 𝟙 [ μ d > 50 ] \sum_{d=1}^{D}\mathds{1}[\mu_{d}>50] ). This yields similar aggregate metrics to the other compliance statistics (precision 0.927 0.927 , recall 0.282 0.282 ), but lacks the probabilistic interpretation.

blocks.en: Additionally, we compute limit-breach statistics from CAMS data for the year 2023. Across all 3060 3060 regulatory NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} monitors, 264 limit breaches were recorded. The CAMS NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} reanalysis with 10 10\text{\,}\, km GSD misses all of the true breaches, estimating limit breaching conditions at none of the regulatory monitor locations (Tab. 9 , Fig. 12 , right). We interpret this as an artifact of averaging highly-varying local NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} levels across the 10 10\text{\,}\, km grid, motivating high-resolution NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} modeling.
blocks.zh: 此外,我们从CAMS数据中计算2023年的限额违反统计。 所有3060 3060 监管NO 2\text{NO\vphantom\text}\smash[t]\text{2}显示器中,记录了264次限制违反规定的情况。 CAMS NO NO\text{NO\vphantom\text}\text{2}用 10\text\\,\\\ km GSD 重新分析所有真实的违反,估计任何监管监视器地点的违反限制条件(图9,图12,右)。 我们将此解读为平均高度变化的本地 NO 2\ text{NO\vphantom\ text}\ text{2} 跨越 10\ text\,\ km 网格, 激发高分辨率 NO 2\ text{NOvphantom\ text}\ text{ text{2} 建模。

blocks.en: 2.3 Air quality zones
blocks.zh: 第2.3条 空气质量区

blocks.en:
Compliance with the EU NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} 24-hour limit is assessed and reported per air-quality zone European Parliament and Council of the European Union (2024) . We obtain zone delineations and their reported resident populations from the EEA e-Reporting portal European Environment Agency (2026) . For each country, we select air quality zones designated for health monitoring and NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} for 2023. Any duplicate zones are removed, and overlaps are resolved by selecting the smallest applicable zone. This results in 670 670 zones across Europe (excluding Switzerland, San Marino, Andorra), with a resident population of 520.8 520.8 M.
To identify breaching zones from modeled hourly NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} concentrations we form daily means from the full-year hourly predictive distribution. We then use the probabilistic compliance statistics to flag any pixels that are estimated to be in breach of the limit. Following the regulatory monitoring convention, a zone is deemed in breach where at least one mapped pixel is flagged. Throughout our analyses, zones are generally mapped only in part, hence the absence of a modeled limit breach only indicates that no exceedance was found within the mapped fraction of the zone, not that the zone as a whole is compliant.
blocks.zh:
遵守欧盟NO 2\ text{NO\vpantom\ text}\smash[t]\ text{2} 每个空气质量区对24小时的限制进行评估和报告 欧洲议会和欧洲联盟理事会(2024年)。 我们从欧洲经济区电子报告门户欧洲环境署(2026年)获得区域划界及其报告的居民人口。 我们为每个国家选择空气质量区, 任何重复区均被移除,通过选择最小的适用区来解决重叠. 这使得全欧洲(不包括瑞士,圣马力诺,安道尔)共有670,670个区,常住人口为520.8,520.8万人.
从模拟的小时NO 2\text{NO\vphantom\text}\text{tsmash}\text{2}中确定突破区,我们每天从全年的小时预测分布中形成能量。 然后我们用概率的遵守统计来标出任何估计违反限额的像素. 根据监管监测公约,至少标出一个映射像素的区域被视为违反规定。 在我们的分析中,一般只绘制了部分区域图,因此,没有模型化的界限突破只表明在所绘制的区域部分内没有发现超过部分,而不是表明整个区域符合规定。

blocks.en: 2.4 Population exposure
blocks.zh: 2.4 人口接触

blocks.en: We translated the predicted exceedance fields into the population living under a predicted breach of the EU 24-hour NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} limit value. For each of the 110 mapped regions we derived a binary breach mask at 10 m 10\text{\,}\mathrm{m} resolution by thresholding the non-compliance probability and combine it with gridded residential population from the Global Human Settlement layer (GHS-POP R2023A) Schiavina et al. (2023) . Each 100 m 100\text{\,}\mathrm{m} population cell contributes its count weighted by the fraction of its area under a predicted breach. Alongside this deterministic estimate we compute an uncertainty-aware count as the expected affected population from the product of the population count and the non-compliance probability. This approach requires no threshold and integrates the model’s per-pixel exceedance probability.
blocks.zh: 我们把预测的超量字段翻译为生活在欧盟24小时NO 2\text{NO\vphantom\text}=smash[t]\text{2}的预计突破值下的人口。 在110个地图区中,我们以10 m 10\ text =, }\ mathrm{ m} 的分辨率, 将不遵守概率设定阈值, 并将其与来自全球人类住区层(GHS-POP R2023A)的网格居民合并。 Schiavina等人(2023年). 每个100 m 100\text\,XQ mathrm{ m} 人口细胞贡献其计数加权值, 以它所在区域在预测的突破下的分数。 除了这一确定性估计之外,我们还计算出对不确定性的认识,即人口计算结果中预期受影响的人口和不遵守概率。 这种方法不需要阈值,并整合模型的每像素超过概率.

blocks.en: 2.5 Breaches on roads
blocks.zh: 2.5 道路越轨事件

blocks.en: Exhaust fumes from vehicles powered by internal combustion engines are one of the main anthropogenic sources of NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} Grice et al. (2009) , and NO 2 \text{NO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} levels are commonly elevated on roads. However, locations at the center of roads or busy intersections are often not representative of the conditions even in the near vicinity. We therefore conduct an analysis where we exclude limit breaches detected on roads explicitly from the obtained results. We obtain road network data from OpenStreetMap OpenStreetMap contributors (2017) and assume road widths at two different levels, narrow and wide (Tab. 10 ), for the road vectors. For this analysis, any limit breaching pixel that intersects with the rasterized road data is disregarded.
blocks.zh: 由内燃机供电的车辆产生的废气是NO 2\text{NO&vphantom\text}\smash[t]\text{2}的主要人为来源之一。 Grice等人(2009年)和NO 2\text{NO\vphantom\text}\smash[t]\text{2}在公路上通常会提高水平。 然而,道路中心位置或繁忙的交叉路口往往不能代表条件,即使在附近地区也是如此。 因此,我们进行分析,将限制在公路上发现的违法行为明确排除在所得结果之外。 我们从OpenStreetMap OpenStreetMap 撰稿人(2017年)处获得道路网络数据,并假定道路宽度为狭长和宽两个不同级别(Tab.10),用于道路矢量. 对于这一分析,任何与光栅化道路数据相交的极限突破像素都不予考虑.
